summary: Update Support macros/runbook: SDK retry/timeout/streaming troubleshooting (post-SDK parity standardization)
description:
Background
- We are shipping cross-language SDK parity updates (Python/TS/Go) for auth precedence, retries/backoff, timeout model, streaming disconnect semantics, and error taxonomy.
- Support is currently using a mix of older macros and ad-hoc questions, which is contributing to slower triage and inconsistent guidance.
- Related: INT-1182 (request_id not visible in SDK errors) is being addressed by SDK changes, but we still need the support workflow updated.

Request
Update Zendesk/Support macros and the internal troubleshooting runbook so that:
1) We ask for the correct minimum set of info (SDK + version, request_id, timeout/retry config, streaming vs non-streaming).
2) Guidance aligns with new standardized option names and defaults (retryable codes, Retry-After behavior, backoff/jitter, overall vs connect/read timeouts).
3) We include streaming-specific guidance (safe retry recommendations, idempotency, partial output expectations).
4) We do not request/collect secrets and we reinforce redaction requirements.

Scope
- Macros to update/add:
  A) "SDK retry/timeout - initial info request" (customer-facing)
  B) "SDK streaming disconnect troubleshooting" (customer-facing)
  C) "SDK 429 / rate limit guidance" (customer-facing)
  D) "Internal triage checklist - SDK failures" (internal note)

Proposed macro content (draft)

A) Customer macro: SDK retry/timeout initial info request
---
To help us diagnose this quickly, could you reply with:
1) Which SDK and version? (Python / TypeScript / Go, e.g. redwood==X.Y.Z)
2) Is this streaming or non-streaming? If streaming, which endpoint/method are you using?
3) A Redwood request_id from a failed attempt (from the error message, response headers, or logs).
4) The approximate timestamp (with timezone) and region where the request was sent.
5) Your configured timeouts and retries (if set):
   - overall timeout (ms or seconds)
   - connect/read timeouts (if your SDK exposes them)
   - max attempts / retry count
   - any custom retryable status codes
6) The HTTP status code(s) observed (e.g., 429/500/502/504) and whether you see a Retry-After header on 429.
7) Any proxy/VPN/corporate network details if applicable (streaming issues often correlate with proxy buffering/timeouts).

Please do NOT paste API keys or bearer tokens. If you share logs, please redact secrets.
---

B) Customer macro: Streaming disconnect troubleshooting
---
For streaming requests, a few extra details help:
1) Are you seeing a disconnect mid-stream (partial output) or no output at all?
2) Is the client behind a corporate proxy or gateway that may buffer/terminate long-lived connections?
3) What is the streaming read/overall timeout configured on the client?
4) If you retry streaming, are you using an idempotency key / request de-duplication strategy? (We generally recommend being conservative with retries for streaming to avoid duplicated side effects.)

If you can share a request_id from the stream attempt (or the last successful event before the disconnect), we can trace it end-to-end.
---

C) Customer macro: 429 / rate limit guidance
---
A 429 indicates you are being rate-limited.
- If the response includes Retry-After, the SDK should respect it by default (newer SDK versions).
- Recommended next steps:
  1) Share the request_id from the 429 response.
  2) Confirm SDK version and whether retries are enabled.
  3) If you run high concurrency, consider lowering parallelism or adding client-side jitter.

If you’re on Dedicated capacity and still seeing sustained 429s, we’ll check capacity/limits for your org.
---

D) Internal note: triage checklist
- Capture: customer tier, workload type (chat/completions/embeddings), streaming yes/no, region.
- Ask for request_id and confirm it’s from the failing attempt (not a successful one).
- Verify SDK version is on or after the parity releases (if not, recommend upgrade + link migration notes).
- Confirm configured timeouts (overall/connect/read). Watch for:
  - overall timeout too low for long prompts/streams
  - streaming read timeout not wired (older versions)
- Confirm retry configuration:
  - ensure no retries on 4xx other than 408/409/429 (per standard)
  - confirm Retry-After handling on 429
- If symptoms suggest retry storm: ask for retry_count / max_attempts, and coordinate with SRE.

Acceptance criteria
- Updated macros published in Zendesk (or equivalent) and linked from the Support runbook.
- Runbook page includes the standardized question set + links to:
  - SDK migration notes (auth/retry/timeout)
  - Retry/timeout standard
  - Auth resolution & secret handling guidance
- Support oncall acknowledges in #support that macros are updated and available.

References
- SDK parity initiative: ENG-5120
- Top support drivers: SUP-29410, SUP-29477, SUP-29505
- Request_id visibility: INT-1182

2026-02-10 09:42 PST — Owen Phillips (Reporter)
Creating this because we’re spending too long in back-and-forth on retry/timeout/streaming tickets. With the parity changes landing, we need macros updated so customers send the right details the first time. Please also ensure we explicitly say “don’t paste API keys” — we’ve had a couple close calls with logs in tickets.

Linking INT-1182 (request_id in errors) and recent customer tickets: SUP-29410, SUP-29477, SUP-29505.

2026-02-11 14:05 PST — Dev Patel (Assignee)
Acknowledged. I’ll draft updated macros + an internal triage checklist and route to Monica/Ibrahim for a quick sanity check on naming/defaults.

Question: do we want the macro to ask for per-SDK config field names, or keep it generic (overall timeout / max attempts / etc.)? I’m leaning generic to avoid drift, with an internal note that maps to each SDK.

2026-02-12 10:18 PST — Ibrahim Khan (SDK parity TL)
Prefer generic in the customer-facing macro. Many customers don’t know the exact field names and it changes across versions.

Internal note can include “where to find it” per language (e.g., client options). Also please add: confirm whether Retry-After was present on 429 and whether they’re behind a proxy if streaming disconnects.

Re: retries — please avoid suggesting “increase retries” as a default fix; for 429 we should prefer respecting Retry-After, lowering concurrency, and adding jitter.

2026-02-13 16:37 PST — Marcus Lin (Security)
+1 to explicit “do not paste API keys/bearer tokens.” Also add a line reminding to redact Authorization headers from HAR files.

If we add any screenshot instructions, ensure we don’t encourage customers to share full environment variable dumps.

I can update the internal runbook page once the macro text is final. Please send the final macro copy + where it will live in Zendesk so I can link it. Also: if there’s a canonical “SDK migration notes” page, send the link/title.
